summary: The per-call vision timeout now divides by the SERIAL factor (the waves one video read awaits in sequence) instead of the media_fetch budget. Dividing a wall-clock ceiling by calls that run CONCURRENTLY shrank it by a factor corresponding to no elapsed time: at the deployment's settings the configured vision_timeout_seconds 120 never took effect, deriving min(120, 360 x 0.6 / 4) = 54 s, and roughly a third of 90-second window reads degraded on the ceiling that existed to prevent exactly that.
details: derive_vision_timeout (nora/infra/vision/client.py) computed `loop * VISION_LOOP_SHARE / max(1, budget)`. `budget` is the number of media_fetch calls a TURN may make and those run concurrently, so they occupy max(their durations) of wall clock, never their sum. The quantity the old invariant proved (budget * derived < loop) was one nothing ever elapses. It now computes `loop * VISION_LOOP_SHARE / max(1, waves)` where `waves = ceil(windows / VISION_WINDOW_CONCURRENCY)`, and the invariant is `waves * derived <= loop * VISION_LOOP_SHARE` — the wall clock one invocation actually consumes. `budget` bounds REFUSALS (R-7's ceiling still comes from ToolRegistry.budgets()); it no longer bounds elapsed time, and it has been removed from the derivation so it cannot come back.

Verified at the deployment's settings (loop 360, configured 120): a one-window read — every Instagram Reel/Story/Post, since VIDEO_CHUNK_SECONDS is 90 — derives 120.0 s, so the configured value is honoured in full; a ten-window read (VIDEO_MAX_CHUNKS, fifteen minutes) derives 21.6 s, so a long clip still cannot outlast the loop. Previously both derived 54 s.

The window count is only known at READ time — cut_video produces it per request, long after VisionClient is built in composition — so the derivation moved into the client, which now holds the derivation's INPUTS (configured, loop_timeout_seconds) and derives per call. `windows` is threaded from read_video_windows (the only place in the codebase that holds the count before the model calls are issued) through a widened two-argument AskWindow protocol, following the existing per-call model/provider/max_bytes seam. No call site computes a timeout itself: single-sourced, because the invariant's own argument is that it must be written down once.

New VISION_WINDOW_CONCURRENCY = 1 is the divisor's companion, written where the derivation can see it, so the bounded asyncio.gather in design/media-read-lane/01-chunk-parallelism.md cannot land without moving the loop and the constant together.

Tests: the regression that would have caught the inert 120 (test_the_derived_timeout_honours_the_configured_value_at_the_instagram_window_count — red at 54.0 on the old formula, green at 120 now); a long clip tightening (10 windows -> 21.6 s); the inverted replacement for the test that PINNED the defect (it asserted budget * derived < loop — now asserting the signature carries no budget at all); the wave invariant parametrised over loop/configured/windows/concurrency with a documented ULP allowance; and a source-reading guard that fails if the window loop fans out while the constant says serial. Full suite: 8688 passed, 12 skipped, 0 failed.
